correctness.rationale: The image of each homomorphism from an elementary abelian 2-group is a totally singular space in the extraspecial quadratic quotient, with exactly 2^r central lifts. Automorphisms surject onto the full orthogonal group by the extraspecial generator presentation. Witt extension plus inner central twists show that the projected kernel K and its central character chi are necessary and sufficient complete orbit invariants. All (K,chi) of codimension no greater than Witt index occur. This proves the Gaussian-binomial orbit formula; the difference of Witt indices proves the first type-distinguishing rank. Classical singular-space enumeration proves the ancillary raw homomorphism formula. Twelve direct automorphism-orbit computations for orders 8 and 32 agree, though the symbolic proof is the general argument.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The general orthogonal quotient and classical totally singular subspace counts apply and are used explicitly, but they give no cited stronger assertion encompassing the full labeled-tuple orbit classification. The motivating Heisenberg calculations concern exponent-p odd characteristic or unconstrained commuting tuples, and do not imply the Arf-type orbit threshold.

value.rationale: Full-automorphism orbit equivalence of elementary abelian representations is a natural invariant of extraspecial groups. The first rank at which the two Arf types have different full-automorphism orbit numbers is exactly the Witt index m (a one-orbit discrepancy), even though their raw involution counts differ at rank one. This is a substantive structural distinction, an exact count for every rank, and an explicit complete orbit classification, not a routine isolated finite census.
